entities.title: JSON request and reply protocol
entities.summary: The request objects afs accepts and the reply fields callers act on, the same through `afs call`, `afs jsonl` and the MCP tools.
consumers: Coding agents, through MCP or a shell, guided by agents/skills/agent-fs/SKILL.md
Developers' shells and scripts using `afs call`
The CI smoke test (`afs call '{"op":"stat","path":"."}'` in .github/workflows/ci.yml)
guarantees: A request is an object whose `op` is read, search, list, stat, outline or diff_since; unknown ops and unknown fields are rejected. An array of requests gets an array of replies in the same order.
Every reply carries `ok`; a failure is {"ok": false, "error": <message>}.
Line numbers and ranges are 1-based and inclusive.
An etag is `b3:` followed by the first 16 hex digits (64 bits) of the content's BLAKE3 hash; equal etags mean equal content.

Replies of read, search, list, outline and diff_since that carry content also carry a `ref` (r1, r2, … per session); a repeat already received is {etag, unchanged: true, ref} with the earlier ref, and `fresh: true` always sends content.
A diff reply carries changed: true, base_etag and hunks of {at, del, new_at, ins}: at is the 1-based old line, del the old lines removed, ins the new text (absent for a pure deletion).
A capped reply carries truncated with next_ranges and bytes_omitted (read) or next_cursor (list); outline and search say truncated.
entities.compatibility: Not stated; waiting on the owner (decisions.json, protocol-compatibility).

entities.title: MCP server and tools
entities.summary: `afs serve` is an MCP server over stdio exposing the six operations as tools afs_read, afs_search, afs_list, afs_stat, afs_outline and afs_diff_since.
consumers: MCP clients that start `afs serve` for a coding agent (the README's .mcp.json entry)
guarantees: Newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 on stdin and stdout; methods initialize, ping, tools/list and tools/call; messages without an id get no reply.
initialize answers with the client's protocolVersion (2024-11-05 when it sends none), the tools capability, serverInfo {name: afs, version: the crate version} and usage instructions.
Each tool's inputSchema lists its fields with additionalProperties false; the tool name minus afs_ is the request's op.
tools/call returns the operation's reply as one text content item holding its JSON, with isError true when the reply is not ok.
Errors: -32700 for a line that is not JSON, -32601 for an unknown method.
entities.compatibility: Not stated; waiting on the owner (decisions.json, protocol-compatibility).

entities.title: Command line and exit codes
entities.summary: The subcommands call, jsonl and serve, where they read and write, and what their exit codes mean.
consumers: The CI smoke test in .github/workflows/ci.yml (`afs --help`, `afs call`)
The zazzle Homebrew formula's test block (`afs --version`), written by macos/release/formula.sh
guarantees: `afs call [JSON|-]` reads the request from the argument, or from stdin when it is omitted or `-`, prints one reply line and exits 0 only when every reply is ok, else 1.
`afs jsonl` and `afs serve` run until stdin closes and exit 0; input that is not UTF-8 ends them with exit code 1.
Errors outside a reply are printed to stderr as `afs: <message>`.
